idiom_name: struct embedding plus per-table Scan functions and a discriminator switch
implementation_notes: Go has no class inheritance, so the mapper hierarchy collapses into hand-written shapes: for Single Table Inheritance one struct carrying all columns plus a switch on the discriminator column that returns the concrete value (a pointer to a struct that embeds the base, or an interface), and for Class Table / Concrete Table Inheritance one Scan target per table with the join written explicitly in the SELECT. database/sql only offers Query/QueryRow plus Rows.Scan, so the load and save functions are the mappers: keep one per table, let callers compose them, and never build SQL by string formatting.
pitfalls: Nullability is per column: nullable subclass columns need sql.NullString/sql.NullInt64, because scanning a NULL into a plain string or int aborts the whole Scan.
db.Query leaks the connection until Rows.Close runs; the deferred Close is easy to drop in a mapper that returns early on Scan errors.
Embedding copies the base struct by value into each derived one: decide deliberately whether identity is shared (pointer to the base) or copied, and keep receivers consistent.
The switch has to be exhaustive by convention only - an unknown kind quietly becomes the base type unless the mapper returns an error.
